{{nihongo|'''Akuto Shrine'''|阿久刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Akuto Shrine''' (あくとじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Seifukuji-chō}}, {{ill|Takatsuki|ar|تاكاتسوكي (أوساكا)|az|Takatsuki|be|Такацукі|bg|Такацуки|ca|Takatsuki|ce|Такацуки|ceb|Takatsuki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Takatsuki|eo|Takatsuki|es|Takatsuki|et|Takatsuki|eu|Takatsuki (Osaka)|fa|تاکاتسوکی|fi|Takatsuki|fr|Takatsuki|ga|Takatsuki|gl|Takatsuki|hu|Takacuki|it|Takatsuki|ja|高槻市|ko|다카쓰키시|mg|Takatsuki|ms|Takatsuki|mzn|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|nl|Takatsuki|no|Takatsuki|pl|Takatsuki|pt|Takatsuki|ro|Takatsuki|ru|Такацуки|sh|Takatsuki|simple|Takatsuki, Osaka|sr|Такацуки|sv|Takatsuki|tg|Такатсуки|th|ทากัตสึกิ|tl|Takatsuki|tr|Takatsuki|tt|Такацуки|uk|Такацукі (Осака)|ur|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|vi|Takatsuki|war|Takatsuki, Osaka|zh|高槻市|zh_classical|高槻市|zh_min_nan|Takatuki-chhī|zh_yue|高槻|qid=Q335423}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sumiyoshi Ōkami}}<ref name="由緒書">Shrine origin document.</ref><ref name="説明板">“Akuto Shrine,” Takatsuki City Board of Education, March 2015 (on-site information board).</ref>
** A collective term for Sokotsutsu-no-Ōno-Mikoto, Nakatsutsu-no-Ōno-Mikoto, and Uwatsutsu-no-Ōno-Mikoto<ref name="由緒書"/>.

Because it is commonly called “Sumiyoshi-san,” the enshrined deity is listed as the Sumiyoshi deity in the *{{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|ja|特選神名牒|qid=Q11571092}}*<ref name="地名">“Place Names of Osaka Prefecture,” entry for Akuto Shrine.</ref>. However, *Setsuyō Gundan* identifies it as a Suwa deity<ref name="地名"/>, while other theories propose Akutohime (consort of {{ill|Emperor Annei|ar|الإمبراطور أنيي|arz|الامبراطور انيى|azb|آنیی (ایمپیراتور)|bg|Аней|ca|Annei|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر ئانێی|cs|Annei|de|Annei|el|Αυτοκράτορας Ανέι|eo|Annei|es|Annei Tennō|fa|امپراتور آنیی|fi|Annei|fr|Annei|he|אני, קיסר יפן|hr|Annei|hu|Annei japán császár|id|Kaisar Annei|it|Annei|ja|安寧天皇|ka|ანეი|ko|안네이 천황|ms|Maharaja Annei|nl|Annei|pl|Annei|pt|Annei|ru|Император Аннэй|sh|Car Annei|simple|Emperor Annei|sl|Cesar Annej|sr|Анеи|sv|Annei|th|จักรพรรดิอันเน|tl|Emperador Annei|tr|Annei|uk|Імператор Анней|uz|Imperator Annei|vi|Thiên hoàng Annei|zh|安寧天皇|zh_classical|安寧天皇|zh_min_nan|Annei Thian-hông|zh_yue|安寧天皇|qid=Q313345}})<ref name="地名"/>, or a deity named Kudo<ref name="歴史館">{{Cite web|ja|year=2012 |url= http://www.city.takatsuki.osaka.jp/rekishi_kanko/rekishi/rekishikan/daionokuni/1327734538892.html |title=Akuto Shrine |work=Internet History Museum |publisher={{ill|Takatsuki|ar|تاكاتسوكي (أوساكا)|az|Takatsuki|be|Такацукі|bg|Такацуки|ca|Takatsuki|ce|Такацуки|ceb|Takatsuki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Takatsuki|eo|Takatsuki|es|Takatsuki|et|Takatsuki|eu|Takatsuki (Osaka)|fa|تاکاتسوکی|fi|Takatsuki|fr|Takatsuki|ga|Takatsuki|gl|Takatsuki|hu|Takacuki|it|Takatsuki|ja|高槻市|ko|다카쓰키시|mg|Takatsuki|ms|Takatsuki|mzn|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|nl|Takatsuki|no|Takatsuki|pl|Takatsuki|pt|Takatsuki|ro|Takatsuki|ru|Такацуки|sh|Takatsuki|simple|Takatsuki, Osaka|sr|Такацуки|sv|Takatsuki|tg|Такатсуки|th|ทากัตสึกิ|tl|Takatsuki|tr|Takatsuki|tt|Такацуки|uk|Такацукі (Осака)|ur|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|vi|Takatsuki|war|Takatsuki, Osaka|zh|高槻市|zh_classical|高槻市|zh_min_nan|Takatuki-chhī|zh_yue|高槻|qid=Q335423}} |accessdate=2015-08-07}}</ref>.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
The founding date is unknown, and several theories have been discussed.

*Shinmyōchō Kōshō* argues a connection with “Akuta,” who is mentioned in the “Tsuki no Muraji” entry of the *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}*<ref>“Shinsen Shōjiroku,” Sakyo Shohan, Tsuki no Muraji entry.</ref>, as someone who presented silk to {{ill|Emperor Kenzō|ar|الإمبراطور كينزو|arz|الامبراطور كينزو|azb|کینزو (ایمپیراتور)|bcl|Emperador Kenzō|cs|Kenzó|de|Kenzō|es|Kenzō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کینزو|fr|Kenzō|hr|Kenzō (japanski car)|hu|Kenzó japán császár|id|Kaisar Kenzō|it|Kenzō (imperatore del Giappone)|ja|顕宗天皇|ka|კენძო|ko|겐조 천황|nl|Kenzo (keizer)|pl|Kenzō|pt|Kenzo|ru|Император Кэндзо|sh|Car Kenzō|simple|Emperor Kenzō|sl|Cesar Kenzo|sv|Kenzo (japansk kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิเค็นโซ|tl|Emperador Kenzō|tr|Kenzō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Кендзо|uz|Imperator Kenzō|vi|Thiên hoàng Kenzō|yo|Emperor Kenzō|zh|顯宗天皇|zh_min_nan|Kenzô Thian-hông|zh_yue|顯宗天皇|qid=Q360966}}<ref name="地名"/>. It further notes that Tsuki no Muraji are recorded as descendants of {{ill|Nuri no Omi|Q119380486|qid=Q119380486}}, identifying him with “Nuri no Mi,” who appears in the *{{ill|Kojiki|ace|Kojiki|ar|كوجيكي|az|Kociki|bcl|Kojiki|be|Кодзікі|bg|Коджики|ca|Kojiki|ckb|کۆجیکی|cs|Kodžiki|da|Kojiki|de|Kojiki|eo|Koĝiki|es|Kojiki|et|Kojiki|eu|Kojiki|fa|کوجیکی|fi|Kojiki|fr|Kojiki|gl|Kojiki|he|קוג'יקי|hi|कोजिकी|hr|Kojiki|hu|Kodzsiki|hy|Կոձիկի|id|Kojiki|it|Kojiki|ja|古事記|ka|კოძიკი|kk|Кодзики|kn|ಕೋಜಿಕಿ|ko|고사기|la|Kojiki|lt|Kodžiki|mk|Коџики|ml|കൊജികി|ms|Kojiki|my|ခိုဂျိခိ|nl|Kojiki|no|Kojiki|oc|Kojiki|pl|Kojiki|pt|Kojiki|ro|Kojiki|rsk|Кодїки|ru|Кодзики|sh|Kojiki|simple|Kojiki|sk|Kodžiki|sl|Kodžiki|sr|Коџики|sv|Kojiki|ta|கோஜிகி|th|โคจิกิ|tl|Kojiki|tr|Kojiki|uk|Кодзікі|vi|Cổ sự ký|zh|古事記|zh_classical|古事記|qid=Q813031}}* as presenting silkworms to the consort of {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|Q313119|qid=Q313119}}. From this, it is inferred that Akuta, an immigrant with sericulture technology, lived in this area and enshrined his clan deity here<ref name="地名"/>.

Another theory points to the “{{ill|Ato no Muraji|Q17191532|qid=Q17191532|lt=Ato no Muraji}},” descendants of {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|Nigihayahi|ja|ニギハヤヒ|simple|Nigihayahi|zh|饒速日命|qid=Q10949054}}, recorded in the Settsu Province section of the *Shinsen Shōjiroku*<ref>“Shinsen Shōjiroku,” Settsu Province, Shinbetsu, Ato no Muraji entry.</ref>, suggesting that the shrine name derives from this clan<ref name="説明板"/>.

It is also said that the name of the {{ill|Akuta River|ja|芥川 (大阪府)|qid=Q11614729}} flowing north of the shrine precincts derives from the shrine’s name<ref name="説明板"/>, changing from “Akutogawa” to “Akutagawa” over time<ref name="歴史館"/><ref>{{Cite book|ja |editor=Haruo Shimomura (ed.) |year=2005 |title=Historical Walk Along the Saigoku Kaidō |publisher=Kansai Historical Walk Association |page=187}}</ref>.

=== Overview ===
The *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}*, compiled in {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}} during the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, lists “Akuto Shrine, {{ill|Shimakami district|ja|島上郡|zh|島上郡|qid=Q10965808}}, Settsu Province,” and ranks it as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}.

Although its subsequent history is unclear, the shrine was burned down during the wars involving the {{ill|Miyoshi clan|Q2975329|qid=Q2975329}} and {{ill|Matsunaga clan|Q11531583|qid=Q11531583}} in the {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} era (1558–1570)<ref name="説明板"/>. The main hall was rebuilt in {{ill|1828|Q7570|qid=Q7570}} (11th year of {{ill|Bunsei|Q1327119|qid=Q1327119}}). During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was known as “Sumiyoshi Daimyōjin.”

Under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Precincts ===
The sacred {{ill|Aphananthe aspera|Q4779482|qid=Q4779482}} standing in the precincts is 21.5 meters tall with a trunk circumference of 3.45 meters<ref>{{Cite web|ja|author=Hideki Kikuchi |url= http://www.city.takatsuki.osaka.jp/ikkrwebBrowse/material/files/group/82/hogojumokuichiran1-2.pdf |format=PDF |title=Protected Trees (List of Protected Trees 1) |work=Designation of Protected Areas (2) Protected Trees |publisher={{ill|Takatsuki|ar|تاكاتسوكي (أوساكا)|az|Takatsuki|be|Такацукі|bg|Такацуки|ca|Takatsuki|ce|Такацуки|ceb|Takatsuki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Takatsuki|eo|Takatsuki|es|Takatsuki|et|Takatsuki|eu|Takatsuki (Osaka)|fa|تاکاتسوکی|fi|Takatsuki|fr|Takatsuki|ga|Takatsuki|gl|Takatsuki|hu|Takacuki|it|Takatsuki|ja|高槻市|ko|다카쓰키시|mg|Takatsuki|ms|Takatsuki|mzn|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|nl|Takatsuki|no|Takatsuki|pl|Takatsuki|pt|Takatsuki|ro|Takatsuki|ru|Такацуки|sh|Takatsuki|simple|Takatsuki, Osaka|sr|Такацуки|sv|Takatsuki|tg|Такатсуки|th|ทากัตสึกิ|tl|Takatsuki|tr|Takatsuki|tt|Такацуки|uk|Такацукі (Осака)|ur|تاکاتسوکی، اوساکا|vi|Takatsuki|war|Takatsuki, Osaka|zh|高槻市|zh_classical|高槻市|zh_min_nan|Takatuki-chhī|zh_yue|高槻|qid=Q335423}} |accessdate=2015-08-08}}</ref>. It was designated a municipal protected tree in {{ill|1990|Q2064|qid=Q2064}} (1st year of {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}})<ref name="歴史館"/>.

=== Auxiliary shrines ===
All are within the precincts.
* Daishōgun Shrine
* Gosha Shrine
* Suwa Shrine
* Kojima Shrine
* Gosha Shrine
* Daishōgun Shrine

=== Festivals ===
* Monthly festival (1st of every month, 10:00 a.m.)<ref>Festival information according to the shrine origin document.</ref>
* New Year’s festival; Great torii chinowa purification ({{ill|January 1|Q2150|qid=Q2150}}–{{ill|January 3|Q2156|qid=Q2156}})
* Tondo festival ({{ill|January 15|Q2260|qid=Q2260}})
* Yakuyoke Setsubun festival ({{ill|February 2|Q2313|qid=Q2313}})
* Doll burning ritual ({{ill|February 3|Q2315|qid=Q2315}})
* Spring festival; yutate ritual (second Sunday of April)
* Autumn festival (October; {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sports Day}})
* Shichi-Go-San visit; wisdom-ring purification ({{ill|November 15|Q2982|qid=Q2982}})

=== Access ===
* From the north exit of {{ill|Takatsuki Station (Osaka)|Q1071995|qid=Q1071995}} on {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|Q502125|qid=Q502125}} (JR West), take the {{ill|Takatsuki City Bus|Q11670759|qid=Q11670759}} bound for Kansai University and get off at “Gunge Hongō” bus stop; 3-minute walk.
